title: Derbent
summary: Derbent is a city in southeastern Dagestan, Russia, in the narrow gap between the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus Mountains. Founded in 438 CE as a fortress guarding a major caravan route, it later passed to Arabs, Tatars and Russians, and its ancient defences became a World Heritage site in 2003.

as_recorded.value: Derbent was founded in 438 ce as a fortress

where.historical_name: Bab al-Abwab ("Main Gate"), or Bab al-Khadid ("Iron Gate") in Arabic

importance.justification: Long-lived fortress city controlling the Caspian-Caucasus passage, now a World Heritage site.

reviewer_note: Sources disagree on founding: Britannica says 438 CE; the Jewish Encyclopedia says the Persian king Khobad founded it at the start of the sixth century, noting an earlier fortified settlement. Russian annexation is given as 1806 (Jewish Encyclopedia) versus 1813 (Britannica). Regions tagging is approximate.
